newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares seen firm in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares seen firm in first quarter.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares are expected to remain on a firm path for the first quarter of 1997 as sentiment continues bullish due to good rains and forecasts of economic growth of seven percent, brokers said on Tuesday.

They and share market analysts however said the Zimbabwean bourse -- which made the third biggest gains on the International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities for 1996 -- was unlikely to surge as high as it did last year.
"We see the market generally rising at a much more gentle pace than we saw in the second half of last year. Last year's performance will be a harder act to follow," one broker said.

"I think the market will continue firm. It's raining and indications are that the rainy season will be normal so the optimism that was expressed on the market last year is certainly still there," said Savvas Kyriakides, managing director of stock and economic analysts Dataworld.

Last year, the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange soared to new record highs, driven largely by investors deserting the local money market where rates have fallen on the back of lower inflation and optimism that the agriculture-driven economy was set for higher growth as weather forecasts indicated normal rains.
The key 57-share industrial index surged 121 percent over the year to end 1996 at an all time peak of 8,786.26.
The bullishness has carried over into the new year and the index has been scaling record levels since its first trading day in 1997 last Thursday, breaking through the 8,900 barrier on Friday.
On Monday, it rose 28.48 points to close at 8,951.13.
"I cannot see the index rising at the same pace as last year based on the fact that institutions now feel that they cannot justify taking prices much higher," another broker said.
"The view is that the quality shares which are the big drivers of the index are fully valued and people are not going to chase them much higher," she added.
Share analyst and columnist Nigel Chanakira said there were some counters which were still undervalued and he saw "a lot of cherry picking" in the first quarter.
He, Kyriakides and other brokers also said they saw local institutional investors continuing to be the main players on the market like they were last year.
"Major foreign investors tend to divorce themselves from the local rain euphoria," one broker said.
